# DeckRenderer

<!-- gen:begin summary -->
<!-- Generated by `npm run generate:op-docs` from noodles-validate/registry.json. The title and the text between gen:begin and gen:end markers are replaced on every run; write anywhere else. -->

Render a deck.gl visualization with layers and effects.
<!-- gen:end summary -->

## Syntax

<!-- gen:begin syntax -->
```json
{
  "id": "/deck-renderer",
  "type": "DeckRendererOp",
  "position": { "x": 0, "y": 0 },
  "data": { "inputs": {} }
}
```

Expressions and code read its fields as `op('/deck-renderer').par.layers` (an input) and `op('/deck-renderer').out.vis` (an output). Edges name the same fields as handles: `par.layers`, `out.vis`.
<!-- gen:end syntax -->

## Remarks

DeckRenderer gathers layers, views, effects, widgets and the basemap into the one visualization the editor shows. The editor shows only the DeckRenderer connected to `vis` on the Out operator at `/out`. Another DeckRenderer, or one that isn't connected there, renders nothing.

`layers` takes any number of connections, and each one adds a layer in connection order. deck.gl draws layers in that order, so the last one connected draws on top.

`basemap` normally comes from [MaplibreBasemap](./maplibre-basemap.md). Its default isn't empty: with nothing connected, DeckRenderer still shows the CARTO Dark Matter style (no labels) over New York at zoom 12. To draw deck.gl layers with no map under them, connect a MaplibreBasemap whose `mapStyle` is empty.

The `longitude`, `latitude`, `zoom`, `pitch` and `bearing` in `viewState` replace the ones that come in through `basemap`, so a camera connected here wins over the one on the MaplibreBasemap. Both are range-checked: a latitude outside -90 to 90, a longitude outside -180 to 180, a pitch outside 0 to 90 or a zoom outside 0 to 24 stops the operator with an "Invalid ViewState" error.

When deck.gl rejects a layer while drawing it, the error goes to the browser console as `[Noodles] Layer error in <layer id>` and the editor keeps running. The layer's node shows no error, so if a layer draws nothing and its node looks fine, check the console.

## Examples

The smallest graph that draws a map: a basemap into a renderer, and the renderer into `/out`.

```json
{
  "nodes": [
    { "id": "/basemap", "type": "MaplibreBasemapOp", "position": { "x": 0, "y": 0 }, "data": { "inputs": {} } },
    { "id": "/deck", "type": "DeckRendererOp", "position": { "x": 300, "y": 0 }, "data": { "inputs": {} } },
    { "id": "/out", "type": "OutOp", "position": { "x": 600, "y": 0 }, "data": { "inputs": {} } }
  ],
  "edges": [
    { "id": "/basemap.out.maplibre->/deck.par.basemap", "source": "/basemap", "sourceHandle": "out.maplibre", "target": "/deck", "targetHandle": "par.basemap" },
    { "id": "/deck.out.vis->/out.par.vis", "source": "/deck", "sourceHandle": "out.vis", "target": "/out", "targetHandle": "par.vis" }
  ]
}
```

Add layers by connecting each layer operator's `out.layer` to `par.layers`.
